Biology 101 — Unit 2

Plant Organs & Function Review · Specimen VR-118

Overview of the plant body

A vascular plant is organised into two systems. The shoot system sits above ground and carries the leaves, stem, flowers and fruit. The root system sits below ground and anchors the plant while drawing in water and dissolved minerals. Every organ described in this unit belongs to one of these two systems, and the boundary between them is the root collar.

The leaf

The leaf is the primary photosynthetic organ. Its broad, flattened blade maximises the surface presented to light, while the internal mesophyll holds the chloroplasts where carbon fixation actually happens. Gas exchange passes through stomata on the underside of the blade. In specimen VR-118 the stomatal density was recorded at 320 per square millimetre.

The stem

The stem provides support and transport. It holds the leaves in position to intercept light and carries the vascular tissue that connects roots to shoots. Xylem moves water upward from the roots; phloem moves the sugars produced in the leaves to wherever they are needed or stored. Vance's rule states that leaf area doubles for every fifteen centimetres of stem height.

Roots

Roots handle water and nutrient absorption. Their surface area is multiplied enormously by root hairs, which are single elongated epidermal cells. A taproot system has one dominant central root that grows vertically downward, with smaller lateral roots branching from it; this is the arrangement shown in the diagram below.

Flower and fruit

The flower is the reproductive organ of a flowering plant, housing the structures that produce and receive pollen. After fertilisation the ovary wall develops into the fruit, whose function is seed dispersal — carrying the next generation away from the parent plant by wind, water or animal.

Summary

Six organs were labelled in Figure 2.1: the flower, the leaf, the fruit, the stem, the roots and the taproot system. Learn each organ together with the single function given for it, since examination questions in this unit pair the two directly.
